newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares buckle under profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares buckle under profit-taking.

text.p: Austrian shares on Thursday were unable to fend off weaker international leads and closed lower, albeit off earlier lows.
The market was weighed down by profit-taking in most blue chips and traders see upside potential in the market limited with consolidation down to 1,220 points on the ATX also a possibility.
"We consolidated -- but it's a positive sign that we didn't close at the day's low," said one trader.
The ATX index lost 7.95 points, or 0.64 percent, to end at 1,241.97 after earlier falling to 1,235.42.
"It was simply profit-taking. If there hadn't have been money coming into OMV at lower levels, then we would've closed a lot lower," said another trader.
Of the ATX's constituents, 17 shares lost ground, three advanced, and one was unchanged.
Among the blue chips, the day's worst performer was cartonboard maker Mayr-Melnhof, losing 2.24 percent to 633.5 ats, while the best was Wolford, up 0.49 percent at 1,433 ats.
In the broader market, the top gainer was Lauda Air , up 14.58 percent at 110 ats, on Wednesday's news rival Austrian Airlines had bought a 36 percent stake in Lauda.
Austrian Airlines added on 3.55 percent to 1,865 ats.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index fell 0.47 percent to 462.79 points.
The March ATX future shed 11.5 points to 1,241 on turnover of 679 contracts.
